findings.title: Readiness panel reports a green "Profile devices — every device is connected" over an empty profile with nothing connected
findings.what_happened: On a fresh profile (My Equipment, 0 devices) with camera/mount/guider all disconnected, the readiness panel shows a GREEN dot on 'Profile devices' with the text 'Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.' The status bar in the same frame reads 'Camera Disconnected  Mount Disconnected  Guider Disconnected'.
findings.expected: With zero devices assigned the row should read 'No devices assigned to this profile' in a neutral/warn state, not a green all-connected pass. A vacuous truth over an empty set is the single most misleading thing a readiness panel can say.
findings.repro: Fresh profile -> Equipment -> 'I'll do it manually' -> right STATUS rail -> 'View all (3 more)' -> read the 'Profile devices' row while the status bar shows every device disconnected.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-09.png (dialog row 'Profile devices' green + 'Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.'; status bar bottom: Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected; profile card reads '0 devices')
findings.proposed_fix: Special-case the empty-assignment case in the profile-devices readiness check: emit a distinct 'no devices assigned' item (warn) instead of the all-connected pass.

findings.title: Dismissing a blocking readiness item hides it while the summary keeps counting it, so the panel claims 3 blockers and lists 2
findings.what_happened: Clicking the X on the blocking 'Critical devices' row (camera not connected) removes the row from the rail, but the summary line above it still reads '3 items are blocking first light.' while only 2 blocking rows remain visible and the hidden one is only reachable via a small 'Show 1 dismissed' link.
findings.expected: Either blocking items should not be dismissable at all (NINA/SGP do not let you hide a hard blocker), or the summary must say '3 blocking (1 hidden)' so the count and the list agree.
findings.repro: Equipment -> right STATUS rail -> click the X on 'Critical devices' -> read the summary line vs the rows shown.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-10.png — summary '3 items are blocking first light.' above only 'Observing location' and 'Capture output folder' blockers plus an amber 'Plate solver'; 'Show 1 dismissed' at the bottom restores it correctly.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude dismissed items from the blocking count, or annotate the count with the hidden total.

findings.title: Shell equipment indicator reads "0/0 — No devices configured" while four devices are connected
findings.what_happened: After connecting Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser and Filter Wheel from Equipment > Discovery, the always-visible status-bar equipment chip still reads '🔭 My Equipment ● 0/0' and its popup body says 'No devices configured'. In the same frame the Equipment header says '4 connected · 4 unsaved', all four device rows say Connected, and the status pills read 'Camera Simulated Camera', 'Mount Simulated Mount', 'Focus 25000'. The count is derived from devices ASSIGNED to the profile, not from what is connected, so any session-only connection (the exact flow the app itself offers with 'This session only — not saved to your profile') is invisible to the shell indicator.
findings.expected: The chip should count live connections, e.g. '4 connected' or '4/0 assigned', and its menu should list the connected devices with a Disconnect for each. Saying 'No devices configured' while four devices are streaming is the shell telling the operator the rig is empty.
findings.repro: Equipment -> 'I'll do it manually' -> Discovery Expand -> Connect on Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser, Filter Wheel -> click the '🔭 My Equipment 0/0' chip at the far left of the status bar.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-17-status-0of0-with-4-connected.png — popup 'My Equipment ● 0/0' + 'No devices configured' next to header '4 connected · 4 unsaved' and four green Connected rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Count connected devices from the device state providers regardless of profile membership; show 'connected/assigned' only when an assignment exists, otherwise 'N connected (session only)'.

findings.title: 'Disconnect All' stays enabled and silently no-ops when nothing is connected
findings.what_happened: With 0 devices connected the equipment-status popup still offers a fully enabled 'Disconnect All' item. Clicking it closes the menu and does nothing — no toast, no log line, no state change.
findings.expected: Disable (grey) 'Disconnect All' when connectedCount == 0, like every other dead action in this build is greyed.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected -> click the equipment chip in the status bar -> 'Disconnect All'. Watch the tree and drive_linux.py log: no change, no message.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-12.png shows 'No devices configured' above a normal-weight (enabled) 'Disconnect All'; the accessibility tree reports 'button: Disconnect All' with no [DISABLED] state; app log shows no entry after the click.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the Disconnect All PopupMenuItem's enabled flag on connectedCount > 0.

findings.title: Guiding-control buttons are invisible to assistive tech: exposed as generic panels with no button role and no disabled state
findings.what_happened: The accessibility tree for the Guiding Controls block reports 'panel: Start', 'panel: Pause', 'panel: Loop Exposures', 'panel: Auto Select', 'panel: Deselect', 'panel: Dither Now' — role 'panel', never 'button', and never [DISABLED] even though all six are logically disabled (onPressed == null) while PHD2 is disconnected. Every other button in the app in the same tree dump reports 'button: <label>' and picks up [DISABLED] correctly (e.g. 'panel: Settle Settings [DISABLED]', 'button: Connect').
findings.expected: These are the controls that start and stop guiding. They should expose a button role and their enabled/disabled state, so a screen-reader user is told 'Start, button, dimmed' rather than a nameless panel.
findings.repro: Guiding screen with PHD2 disconnected -> drive_linux.py tree -> read the Guiding Controls subtree.
findings.evidence: tree output at 14:41 shows 'panel: Start / panel: Pause / panel: Loop Exposures / panel: Star Selection / panel: Auto Select / panel: Deselect / panel: Dither' with no roles or states; the same dump has 'button: Connect' and 'panel: Settle Settings [DISABLED]' so the harness does read roles and states when they are published.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/phd2/guide_controls_panel.dart (_actionButton builds a bare Material+InkWell with no Semantics(button: true, enabled: ...))
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the InkWell in Semantics(button: true, enabled: !isDisabled, label: label) or use the design-system button widget that already publishes those flags.
